entry.title: A few words, then time to respond
entry.summary: A short, useful cue can be easier to act on than repeated instructions. Give your child time, and show what you mean if the words are not enough.
entry.cue: You have asked more than once, and your child has not yet begun.
detail: Davies suggests a brief piece of information or a familiar word, such as pointing out where something belongs. Go over and show the place if your child seems unsure.
A pause can leave room for processing. She also suggests saying what the child can do, rather than repeatedly describing what to stop.

For a necessary transition, she states what is happening kindly instead of asking a question with no real choice. Gentle humor is another possibility, such as pretending a child’s shoe fits your foot. None of these needs to work every time.

references.locator: Useful information, one word, positive language, humor, no phase, show action and processing time
